title: Word Break
keyIdea: dp[i] = can the first i letters be split into dictionary words. dp[0] = true. dp[i] = true if some word w ends at i (s[i − |w| .. i) == w) and dp[i − |w|] is true. Answer dp[n].

approaches.name: Prefix DP over words
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). dp[0] = true; for each i, try every word as the last word ending at i.
approaches.why: n positions × W words × an O(L) compare.

options: The first i letters can be split into words
Letter i is in a word
The suffix from i can be split
The empty prefix needs no words

quiz.q: Why does plain recursion blow up on "aaaaaaab" with ["a","aa","aaa"]?
options: It retries the same suffix in many ways; dp solves each prefix once

steps: Words can be reused? Dictionary size and word lengths?
Brute force: try every first word recursively. Cost?
"Can the string be cut into dictionary pieces" → prefix DP.
Plan dp[i] and the last-word check.
Time and space? Trie or set alternatives?
